title: OpVariant hyperheuristic: architecture & sequence-length aware routing for attention kernels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The serving runtime currently picks attention kernel variants via a static lookup that does not generalize across GPU families, token phase (prefill vs decode), or mixed-length workloads. This causes 95th percentile latency spikes and suboptimal cost on heterogenous fleets. Goal: build a lightweight hyperheuristic that routes requests to op variants based on architecture fingerprint, sequence-length bucket, and request phase (prefill/decode) with safe online autotuning and fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency reduced by >= 10% on mixed-length conversational workload compared to baseline in benchmark cluster
Median token cost reduced by >= 6% on reserve-Dedicated traces
No increase in error rates or correctness regressions (validated by existing unit tests and eval prompt set)
Canary rollout with automatic rollback on >10% degradation in P95 within 1 hour
Dashboard shows per-arch, per-seqlen decision distribution and estimated cost delta
technical_approach: Two-stage decision pipeline: 1) coarse bucketizer by (GPU_arch, model_variant, effective_seq_len, phase) using deterministic rules; 2) lightweight online tuner per bucket that hedges between top-3 opvariants via contextual bandit with exponential smoothing for telemetry noise.
Offline component: dense microbench grid (arch x seqlen x batch x opvariant) to seed priors and cold-start bands; results persisted to kernel-catalog metadata store.
Runtime agent: assign each request to bucket, consult cached bandit policy; when policy confidence < threshold, issue a probe sample with bounded probe rate and throttle to avoid perturbing SLOs.
Safety: enforce latency budget per request using model of probe cost; always keep a low-latency fallback opvariant pinned for SLO-critical tiers.
Lightweight model: XGBoost-style gradient tree on offline features for initial ranking; online bandit uses Thompson sampling with Gaussian reward model for simplicity and explainability.
Instrumentation points added to request path to capture variant_id, probe_flag, raw_latency_ms, decode_step, token_count, kv_cache_hit, and occupant_count.
Config surface: feature flags for global enable, per-customer enable, probe_rate, and per-bucket exploration epsilon.
experiments_plan: Stage 0 - Offline sweep: run microbench across target GPU SKUs (A100, H100, 4090-equivalents) and seqlens {32,64,128,256,512} to compute baseline cost/latency per opvariant (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime-microbench#42)

Stage 1 - Shadow evaluation: run decision engine in shadow mode for 48h on production-like traffic in staging cluster and record what it would have chosen vs actual; compare latencies in offline replay.
Stage 2 - Canary: enable on 5% traffic for non-SLA test tenants with probe_rate=0.02 and fallback pinning; monitor P50/P95 and cost metrics for 24h.
Stage 3 - Progressive rollout with doubling cadence and automated rollback if P95 regresses by >10% or error-rate increases >2x.
Benchmarks to run: conversational-mix (60% decode short-turns, 40% long prefill), batch-embeddings worst-case, and tail-latency stress tests.
telemetry: Emit per-request records with fields: timestamp, cluster, node_type, gpu_arch, model, opvariant_id, seqlen_bucket, phase, latency_ms, tokens_generated, probe_flag, decision_confidence
Aggregate metrics: per-minute histogram of latency per opvariant, traffic share by variant, probe success rate, fallback invocations
New dashboards: 'OpVariant Decision Map' (heatmap by arch x seqlen), 'Probe Safety' (probe rate vs P95), and 'Cost delta by decision'
Logging: sample traces for decisions that led to >2x baseline latency for postmortem; include GPU metrics (SM utilization, memory bandwidth) from node exporter
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout starting in us-west-2 staging cluster
Canary cohort: non-SLA customers and internal test tenants only, initial traffic 5%
Monitoring window: automatic health check every 10 minutes, alarm if P95 increases >10% or error-rate >2x
Auto-rollback: lambda that flips feature flag and marks bucket as unsafe for 2h; team notified in #runtime-ops
Full rollout: expand to Dedicated pools after 2 successful 24h canaries; runtime-1.20 release notes updated
risks: Telemetry noise: GPU contention can bias probe measurements leading bandit to converge to suboptimal choices
Cold-start buckets: rare arch+seqlen combinations may not have enough data — mitigate with stronger offline priors and conservative fallback
Interference: probes may increase tail latency if not throttled; must enforce strict probe caps per node
Complexity: adding many per-bucket policies increases config surface and maintenance burden
Model-change regressions: upgrades to opvariant implementations could invalidate priors — include model-signature in bucket key
